newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium physicals firming, Russian availability.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium physicals firming, Russian availability.

text.p: Premiums in the European physical aluminium market have started 1997 on a strong note, with business picking up and Russian metal in short supply, traders said.
Also, reports of high premium levels elsewhere, particularly in the U.S. Midwest, are underscoring the trend, with aluminium being diverted away from Europe, they said.
"People are not shipping it (Russian metal) to Europe...it is going instead to the Far East and the U.S.," one said.

And as overall activity has picked up markedly, premiums have risen by some $10/15 for both Western origin and Russian LME-deliverable aluminium. Russian off-grades, meanwhile, are also running at appreciable premiums to the terminal now.

"Business has improved quite dramatically, and because many (users) had run down their stocks to very low levels any pick-up in demand was bound to filter through into premiums very quickly," another trader said.
In many cases, some consumers were living off stocks built up in 1995, and these have now been eroded.
"I think that both the first quarter and the second quarter are going to be very good," the trader added.
The trend also reflects the macro-economic picture - with economic activity in general on an upswing and likely to continue throughout the year.
But some traders were unsure, however, and said that the current strength in the LME and the physical market may not be maintained.
"I think it is a case of these big Midwest premiums sucking metal away...From what I hear the forward premiums are not moving higher as well," one said.
Although traders are reporting that Midwest aluminium is trading at 4.75 cents/lb, there is some talk of material being asked as high as 5.50 cents/lb.
In Europe, the shortage of Russian aluminium has resulted in off-grade A6 and A5 business at levels of $30 and $25 over the LME respectively.
Russian A0, which is 99.00 percent purity, is now around level to the LME, while 97 percent and 96 percent purity Russian is being transacted at respective discounts of $50 and $85, traders report.
As well as being switched to other areas, there is also less off-grade Russian aluminium being produced and shipped now, as smelting techniques have improved in recent years, traders noted.
